name: Vibrate the device
plain: Triggers the phone's vibration motor in short pulses.
meaning: A site can buzz the device for feedback or alerts. It is Android only, needs a tap first, and cannot run from hidden frames or background tabs.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: One-shot pattern; cancelled by vibrate(0) or tab hide
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Blocked in cross-origin iframes without prior activation in that frame (Firefox 72, Chrome 77)
steps: Person taps in the page (sticky activation in the frame)

limits.headline: Can buzz the phone in short pulses, after you have tapped the page
limits.user_action: You tap a button, win a game, or touch the page before it buzzes.
can: Buzz your Android phone in a pattern after a tap
Give touch feedback in games and timers
cannot: Buzz without any earlier tap on the page
Buzz on iPhone, because Safari does not offer it
Buzz in current Firefox, which no longer offers it
limits.differs: Android Chrome and Edge allow it. iPhone Safari does not.

story.what_it_is: A site can make your phone buzz in short bursts after you tap.

marketing.name: Vibration API
marketing.pitch: MDN says the Vibration API lets a page buzz the phone for feedback.

story.for_you: You tap a button in a web game or app and feel a short buzz. Safari on iPhone does not allow it, so you only feel it on some phones.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for touch feedback that makes a web app feel like a real app. It is cheap and needs no permission, only a recent tap.

use_cases.example: A browser racing or shooter game buzzes when you crash or get hit.
A web chat app buzzes your phone for a new message when it is open.
A checkout page buzzes once when the payment goes through.
A workout timer buzzes at the end of each set.
A web app buzzes to confirm a tap for people who cannot see well.
An annoying ad may try to buzz the phone to get attention, which Chrome blocks without a tap.

technical_bounds: Needs sticky user activation in the frame (Chrome 60); no prompt
Pattern limited to 99 entries and 10 s per entry in Chrome (about); longer values truncated
Not available in Safari or any iOS browser; Firefox desktop removed it in 129
Stops when the tab is hidden or screen locks
Hardware intensity cannot be set; only on and off durations

history.change: Cross-origin iframe vibrate needs activation in that frame
Vibration API removed from desktop Firefox
